title: Shrill, with deep laughter, after, gold after bronze, they urged each each to peal after peal, ringing in changes, bronzegold, goldbronze, shrilldeep, to laughter after laughter. And then laughed more
html_source: “[A]n exuberance of character gives rise to an exuberance of language” (Christopher A. Strathman. Romantic Poetry and the Fragmentary Imperative: Schlegel, Byron, Joyce, Blanchot, p137). Strathman analyses the paragraph stating that Joyce has been building up to this episode, preparing the reader, throughout Ulysses and now overthrows the narrative by use of interlacing sounds – the word wins ; ‘laughter after laughter’ could easily be lafter aughter lafter.
